messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — sev2: increased 5xx and timeouts observed for egress from AZ-d (eu-central-1d). Auto-threshold triggered. Paging oncall.

incident-bot: Affected services: hosting-api, embedder, batch-encoder. Region: eu-central-1, AZ: d. Start: 2026-03-15T09:12:34Z.

tess: oncall here, diving in. 5xx spike looks correlated with NAT gateway metrics in az-d. tagging a bridge: #incident-bridge-3399123456.

ryan: seeing similar in logs — a lot of TCP RST/timeout from our side when trying to reach tokenization microservices out to internet.

maya: routing tables for private subnets in az-d were modified ~09:05Z by a terraform apply from infra-ci. Possible relation.

sam: grabbing quick instrumentation:
```
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0a1b2c3d --region eu-central-1
```
results show a 0.0.0.0/0 route pointing to rt-0fdeadbeef (peering) instead of nat-0abc12345.

netops: that matches a bad plan we saw earlier — duplicate route propagation from a transient peering route leaked into subnet route table. Peering was being tested and has no egress path, so outbound traffic blackholed.

tess: immediate mitigation: re-attach route to nat gateway. sam, can you run the rollback? If not, we'll add a higher-priority explicit 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0abc12345 route.

sam: running:
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-01234567 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-0abc12345 --region eu-central-1
```

sam: confirmed replaced route in rtb-01234567. Pushing a small canary.

maya: I'm seeing 5xx rate drop in az-d from ~18% -> ~3% in the last 40s. Latency still elevated but degrading.

ryan: rerouting traffic to az-b for critical requests via smart-routing policy (failover) — toggled to route ~40% away from az-d to reduce customer impact.

customer-success: FYI we got two customer escalations (enterprise customers A+B) reporting degraded API responses since ~09:10Z. I told them we're investigating and routing traffic; will follow up with timeline and mitigation summary.

netops: need to confirm root cause: the peering route had been set to propagate (auto-prop) by mistake during test. That caused a duplicate 0.0.0.0/0 entry with the same prefix but an unexpected target. When AWS evaluates route priority, explicit local route to peering took precedence in this account/setup.

tess: good catch. We need a short action list: 1) Confirm revert complete and all subnets in az-d have nat route. 2) Block route propagation for that peering connection. 3) Re-run terraform with a guard. 4) Communicate ETA to customers.

sam: running a sweep:
```
for rtb in $(aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=tag:az,Values=eu-central-1d --query 'RouteTables[].RouteTableId' --output text); do aws ec2 describe-route-tables --route-table-ids $rtb --query 'RouteTables[].Routes[]' --output json; done
```
All private subnets now show 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0abc12345.

maya: NACL/SG looks unchanged — no additional port blocking. So this was purely a route priority/propagation issue.

ryan: confirm from metrics: host-api 5xx from az-d back to baseline ~2.1% and p95 latency improved. Still monitoring for error bursts.

incident-bot: NOTE — followup action required: add terraform guard to prevent route-propagation flag on peering resources.

netops: I'm disabling route propagation on pcx-0feedface now.

netops: done — propagation disabled. Also added a lock-tag to the peering resource to prevent accidental apply.

sam: prepping a small terraform apply to enforce expected route table associations: `terraform apply -target=aws_route_table_association.private-azd -auto-approve`

maya: rolling that now, will avoid touching peering.

maya: apply completed. Validate: all private subnets in az-d reference rtb-01234567 which points to nat-0abc12345.

customer-success: shared an interim note to affected customers: "We've identified a routing regression caused by a peering test route propagation and applied an immediate fix to restore NAT egress. We're monitoring and will follow up with a postmortem." They asked for an ETA for full RCA.

tess: ETA for initial RCA draft — 3 hours. Full postmortem with timeline and remediation steps — EOD.

ryan: next tasks: add CI gate to detect changes that enable route propagation on peering, and add a monitoring rule to alert if default route target != expected nat gateway for prod subnets.

netops: adding a config rule to check route-table default route targets. I'll open a PR now.

sam: any customer-impacting retries we need to run? Some queued jobs will recover once egress restored. We'll throttle replay to avoid overload.

tess: handoff to night oncall @ 12:00Z in 2 hours. @ryan please keep monitoring until then; @maya file the terraform guard PR and link here.

maya: PR opened: https://git.internal/rw/infra/pull/1987 — adds explicit `propagate = false` on test peerings and a policy preventing `aws_vpc_peering_connection_options` from being set to propagate on prod tags.

ryan: monitoring looks clean for now. No new customer reports after the note went out.

customer-success: updated customers A+B with mitigation timeline and expected RCA window. They acknowledged.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS — mitigated. Monitoring. Severity will be downgraded after two hours of stable metrics.

tess: thanks everyone. We'll collect logs and make the postmortem. If anything flares, re-open this thread.

sam: capturing runbook notes into the incident doc and attaching route-table dumps.

netops: one follow-up: we should add a pre-apply terraform plan check that greps for `route_propagation` changes on peerings; can be a cheap safety net.

maya: will include that in the PR.

ryan: handing off to next oncall — @sam you're point for overnight monitoring. I'll catch-up in the morning for postmortem edits.

sam: ack.

incident-bot: HANDOFF — active oncall changed: tess -> sam at 2026-03-15T11:59:00Z.
